title: Rebaseline: narrow console observability to guaranteed core metrics and graceful fallbacks
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Context: As part of the Console telemetry rebaseline, we must reduce scope so we can ship a small, reliable observability surface that gives product teams predictable insight into runtime health and cost without committing to the full roadmap of card permutations, deep trace UX, and per-token drilling features. Goal: deliver a hardened set of console capabilities that cover operational needs (SLO indicators, error budget visibility, cost per-route summary) and provide automated fallback behaviors when detailed instrumentation is not yet available. This ticket defines what we cut, what we guarantee, acceptance criteria, and the runbook for engineering/design handoff.
scope_changes: Keep: six core dashboard cards (global throughput, 95th latency, p99 on-demand alert, error-rate, route-level cost-per-minute, model-variant availability). These are implemented as aggregated rollups only (no token-level drilldowns).
Cut: per-token cost traces, per-call token breakdown, and expanded time-series explorer. These will be moved to a post-MVP epic (Tracking: PM-41258).
Keep: lightweight trace sampling at request-level with span linking for failed requests only; postpone full span visualization and flamegraphs to a later milestone.
Cut: advanced trace search (by custom attributes) — provide a simple indexed failure-id lookup instead.
Keep: an automatic fallback policy for routes whose telemetry is degraded: show last-known aggregates with a warning banner and link to troubleshooting playbook.
Cut: interactive anomaly detection in this release; include manual thresholds and exportable CSVs for analysts instead.
Constraint: cost breakdown will be per-route aggregated token-minute buckets (1m granularity) rather than per-token microbilling UI to reduce cardinality and storage footprint.
decision_log: 2026-03-10 — PM kickoff: Decided to prioritize operational signal over exploratory analytics. Trade-off: less exploratory power for faster time-to-stable-release.
2026-03-11 — Eng constraints review: Kernel selection telemetry increases cardinality by 12x; agreed to aggregate by model-variant instead of per-kernel to stay within budget (ENG-4219).
2026-03-12 — Design critique: deep trace UX requires additional infra and is out-of-scope for this cycle; suggested failure-id focused UX for fast debug loops.
2026-03-13 — Final decision: Ship the six-card surface + sampled traces for failures + fallback banner. Record acceptance criteria and handoff artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: 6 core cards render within 500ms on first load for accounts with <= 10 routes. Metrics: global throughput, p95 latency, error rate, p99 latency alerts, route-level cost-per-minute, model-variant availability.
Cost surface: per-route aggregated cost is shown in 1-minute buckets for the last 24 hours and last 7 days with export CSV option. No per-token UI present.

Tracing: For failed requests (error >= 500 or user-defined threshold), a sampled trace is captured with a failure-id. UI allows searching by failure-id and opening the linked minimal trace view (spans collapsed by default).

Fallback behavior: If telemetry ingestion for a route is delayed > 2 minutes or fails, UI shows last-known aggregates with a yellow warning banner and a single-click "Open troubleshooting playbook" link.
Storage & cost: Telemetry pipeline budget must not increase by more than 20% compared to baseline; infra runbook updated and approved by ENG infra owner (ENG-4219).

Ownership & docs: Handoff bundle (API contracts, sample payloads, dashboard mocks, acceptance e2e playbook) uploaded to Confluence and linked in this ticket. Engineering signs off in code review referencing the release tag console-2026.04.
Telemetry quality: SLO for the surface: 99.5% of dashboard API calls return within 500ms for permitted accounts; synthetic tests in CI confirm this before release.
